# The desktop as a command workspace

*Plan of record for the Option B desktop redesign. Written against `d716047`, verified at that commit; the reference is `goose` at `3810898a7`.*

Baseline this plan has to beat, run at HEAD before writing a line of it:

```
node docs/audit.js both
Clean: no geometry findings across 98 phone states x 2 themes x 6 phone sizes
(320x568/360x800/375x667/390x844/402x874/440x956) x 4 text sizes (16/17/23/53px),
and 28 desktop states x 2 themes x 7 window sizes
(480x560/571x700/572x700/901x760/902x760/1180x820/1600x1000) x 1 text size (16px)
x 3 shell states (nav open/nav closed/nav open fullscreen)
```

`docs/gallery-states.json` holds 63 keys — 49 phone, 14 desktop. The audit doubles each with a stress variant (`docs/audit.js:1540`), which is where 98 and 28 come from.

---

## 1. THE SHAPE

The three columns stay — nav, list, detail — and what the redesign adds is a **fourth plane and a new kind of value**. The value is a `Command`: a `Copy` struct of `{ id, label, icon, action }` that travels the way `nav::Crumb` already travels, so the thing a screen *can do* reaches the window's bar even though Dioxus has no portal and `docs/design.md:1464` is right that "`.topbar-actions` is an `Element`, which is the one thing that cannot travel." A command is data, and data travels. The plane is `.layer` — one `position: fixed` sibling inside `.shell` holding at most one anchored popover, which is the markup `assets/desktop.css:1158-1159` says outright the shell does not own and which every remaining capability needs: the band's session actions, the row overflow anchored to its own `⋯` instead of 1,224pt away, the model picker, the working-directory switcher, the extension menu. On top of that primitive the app grows *depth inside destinations* rather than more destinations — Settings gains a section index in the list column, Code's list column starts following its own stack instead of showing the session list beside a diff — and then a menu bar generated from `nav::DESTINATIONS`, then the composer's six satellite controls, then a live chats feed in the nav, and last a deck of live sessions in `src/state.rs`. Nothing in Rust ever listens to a resize; every affordance is still chosen by `target_os` in `src/shell/`; the phone's 49 captured states are untouched until one deliberate, budgeted device run.

## 2. WHY THIS AND NOT THE OTHER TWO

**Against reference-first.** That proposal's premise is verified — `ui/desktop/src/components/Layout/AppLayout.tsx:126-157` really is a nav column and exactly one `<div className="flex-1 overflow-hidden min-h-0">`, and `SchedulesView.tsx:471-477` really does return the detail *instead of* the list — and our own tree concedes it twice in prose (`src/shell/desktop.rs:406-411`, `assets/desktop.css:435-440`). But the reference's layout is the least desktop-shaped part of an app the user named for its *functionality*: it is a react-router SPA with one `<Outlet/>`, and it has no second column to place because it has no list to place. We already have the Mac idiom — source list plus content — and collapsing it would take side-by-side list+detail away from Code, Recipes, Skills, Scheduler and Extensions to give it to Chats. Worse for the way this repo works: that collapse is a user-visible product bet taken in the *first* commit, and the proposal itself concedes the audit cannot see it ("One column and two columns are both valid layouts; nothing overflows, nothing collides"), while the same commit deletes `901×760` and `902×760` from `DESKTOP_SIZES` (`docs/audit.js:532-540`) — the two sizes chosen to straddle the breakpoint being removed. **What it was right about, and what this plan takes:** (a) the store-reading gate that every `nav::DESTINATIONS` id must have a `desktop-<id>…` key, paired with hardening `docs/audit.js:1694-1695`; (b) that multi-session is a `Signal<HashMap<…>>` beside `ctx.chat` and *not* the reference's ten mounted-and-hidden `BaseChat`s, because `src/state.rs:687` is already one pump over one socket and `:691-694`'s `if !is_current { continue; }` is the only thing dropping background sessions; (c) the nav's live CHATS section (`NavigationPanel.tsx:317-408`, `MAX_RECENT_SESSIONS = 25` at `useNavigationSessions.ts:14`), which is the single most desktop-shaped affordance the reference has. All three are in the sequence below. **And it may yet be right about the columns** — Stage G is written so that its per-destination opt-in is the design rather than a recovery.

**Against phone-divergence.** It did the best measurement work of the three and two of its numbers reproduce exactly: the desktop half of the store renders 14 hamburgers and 16 connection badges that are painted to nothing, and `desktop-settings`'s `<header class="topbar">` has four children of which every one is invisible. That ledger is real and this plan uses it. But the case it makes is plumbing, not capability: five consecutive stages convert compiler-checked shared markup into two hand-maintained renderers, and the finished app has no menu bar, no accelerators, no search, no settings depth, none of the six `ui/desktop/src/components/bottom_menu/` controls, and — explicitly refused — no multi-session. Its own §7(1) says "if you measure this in lines, it loses." Two of its load-bearing claims also fail on inspection: its Stage 2 premise that "nothing on the desktop calls `TopBar`/`ListRow` any more" is false, because those are called from `views/sessions.rs`, `views/recipes.rs`, `views/skills.rs`, `views/extensions.rs` and `views/scheduler.rs` — which are exactly what the desktop's list column renders; and its "proven failure" that deleting the `.navpane` collapse block leaves `cargo test` green is wrong, because `[data-nav="closed"]` appears only at `assets/desktop.css:229` and `:236`, so `the_stylesheet_acts_on_the_attribute_the_shell_sets` (`src/shell/desktop.rs:864`) reddens immediately. **What it was right about, and what this plan takes:** (a) the pane header should stop *rendering* the title, hamburger and badge rather than have them hidden in CSS — a hidden control the audit still walks is a control nothing checks; (b) a test that reads the *desktop* half of the store, asserting `seen > 0` so an emptied half cannot pass vacuously — verified as a genuine first, since `DUMP_PREFIX_DESKTOP` has exactly one non-`mod.rs` use today (`src/views/chrome.rs:530`) and it is a `!starts_with` filter; (c) both of its phone findings, in §5. **And it may yet be right about the seam** — if Stage F's composer work turns into `Shell::CURRENT` branches scattered through `views/chat.rs`, its per-component split is the answer, and its ledger is the measurement that would justify it.

## 3. THE FIRST COMMIT

### "The window's bar does what it names."

The command primitive, and the band painting the one command a chat already has. It deletes nothing, moves no column, and every command it introduces is a second route to a control already on screen.

**One repair to the winning proposal, stated up front, because it is the reason this commit is buildable at all.** The original scope had the band drive *rename* and *delete* on the open chat. It cannot: `src/views/chat.rs:88-92` holds `sheet`, `mode_sheet`, `confirm_delete`, `rename` and `menu` as view-local `use_signal`s inside `ChatView`, which `nav.rs:232` mounts as a **descendant** of `AppShell` — a parent cannot read or write a child's `use_signal`. Making that work means lifting them onto `AppCtx`, i.e. editing `src/state.rs`, the file every live worktree merges into, in commit 1 for zero user-visible gain. So commit 1's commands are the ones whose action is a **free function over `&AppCtx`**, and there are two: `crate::state::new_session` (`src/state.rs:1382`) and a `ctx.code_screen` write (`src/state.rs:375`). Rename and delete arrive in Stage C, behind the popover, where the state they need is being moved anyway.

**Second repair.** The original scope collapsed `REFRESH_KEY` (`src/shell/desktop.rs:85`), `DISMISS_KEY` (`:132`) and `NAV_KEY` (`:173`) into one generated listener. Read them: they are three different programs, not three chord rows. `REFRESH_KEY` enumerates `[data-refresh]` and sends N messages; `DISMISS_KEY` sends nothing to Rust at all and runs the `p.modal-body` discriminator that exists specifically so Escape does not answer a permission prompt with "Always allow" (`:118-127`); `NAV_KEY` matches a character with no shift guard because reaching `/` requires Shift on most of Europe (`:161-166`). A `{id,label,icon,action}` table cannot emit those bodies, keyboard JS is invisible to the audit grid, and this is the app's only Escape route out of a modal. **The three strings are untouched by this commit and by this plan.** Accelerators arrive in Stage E as *declarations* the menu bar renders, checked against those strings by a test, not as a generator of them.

### Files

| file | change |
|---|---|
| `src/command.rs` | **new.** `Command { id, label, icon, action }`, `#[derive(Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]`; `enum Action { NewChat, NewCodeSession }`; `fn Action::perform(self, ctx: &AppCtx)`. No `danger` and no `accel` yet — nothing declared that is not implemented. A compile-time `Copy` bound (`const _: fn() = \|\| { fn c<T: Copy>() {} c::<Command>(); };`) is the guard against the failure mode the winning proposal named in its own §7: the day `Command` grows a `Custom(Element)` variant, an `Element` is living in a struct the phone compiles and `docs/design.md:1464` has been defeated by the back door. An `Element` is not `Copy`, so that line fails the build. |
| `src/nav.rs` | `Detail` gains `pub commands: &'static [Command]`, carrying **verbatim** the `#[cfg_attr(any(target_os = "ios", target_os = "android"), expect(dead_code, …))]` that `crumb` already carries at `:80-87`. `Detail::new` (`:92-94`, a `const fn`, 10 call sites) defaults it to `&[]`, so every existing site is untouched; a `const fn Detail::with(self, commands)` is how a row opts in. Two rows opt in: `CHATS`'s `Screen::Chat` arm (`:230-233`) → `&[NEW_CHAT]`, and Code's `CodeScreen::Chat` arm (`:275-278`) → `&[NEW_CODE_SESSION]`. |
| `src/shell/desktop.rs` | `.chrome-actions` in `header.shell-chrome`, between `.chrome-title` (`:490-497`) and `.window-drag` (`:519-529`) — beside the title, the way `SessionActionsHeader.tsx:551` puts its actions beside the title. Painted from `detail.commands`; `class: "chrome-action"` as a **literal**, not a compound and not a conditional (see the gate below). `detail` is already read at `:399`. |
| `assets/desktop.css` | `.chrome-actions { flex: 0 0 auto; margin-top: var(--chrome-pad); height: 32px; display: flex; gap: 4px }` and `.chrome-action` in `.nav-toggle`'s shape. **No narrow-tier rule.** The band's shrink order is already title-first — `.chrome-title` is `flex: 0 1 auto; min-width: 0` (`:304-305`) and `.window-drag` is `flex: 1 0 96px` (`:369`) — so two 32px buttons come out of the title's ellipsis and not the drag strip. Whether ≤571 needs a rule is a question the audit answers, not one to guess. |
| `docs/audit.js` | **Two changes, both closing holes that are open today.** (1) `:1046`'s TITLE-COLLIDE selector list is `':scope > .icon-btn, :scope > .topbar-actions, :scope > .nav-toggle, :scope > .conn-badge'` — `.chrome-actions` is not in it, so without this the check is blind to exactly the element being added. It gains `:scope > .chrome-actions`. (2) `:1694-1695`'s `const shell = document.querySelector('.shell'); if (!shell) return;` becomes a throw on a `desktop-`-keyed state. |
| `src/shell/desktop.rs` tests | two new tests, below. |
| `docs/design.md`, `CLAUDE.md` | the band's fourth slot; the calibration table gains its row. |

**Not edited, and this is the review rule: `git diff --stat` must not name `src/views/`, `src/shell/mobile.rs`, `src/shell/mod.rs`, `src/state.rs`, `assets/main.css` or `assets/features/`.**

### Gates, each with the way to make it fail

| gate | make it fail |
|---|---|
| `cargo test --workspace`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --all -- --check` | — |
| `cargo check -p goose-mobile --target aarch64-apple-ios` | have any phone-compiled path read `Detail::commands`. The `expect(dead_code)` becomes unfulfilled and CI's `-D warnings` reddens. This is the mechanism `nav.rs:80-87` already runs for `crumb`, unchanged. |
| `every_class_the_shell_renders_is_styled_somewhere` (`src/shell/desktop.rs:727`) gains `"chrome-actions"` and `"chrome-action"` | **Two directions, and the trap is real.** Rename `.chrome-action` to `.chrome-act` in the sheet → red, because the boundary check at `:738-746` requires the character after `.chrome-action` not be `[a-z0-9-_]`, and `.chrome-actions` (an `s`) does **not** satisfy it. And emit `class: "chrome-action btn"` instead of the bare literal → red, because `:760` is `shell.contains(&format!("class: \"{class}\""))`. A compound class name would have silently failed this gate. |
| **NEW** `the_window_bar_paints_the_commands_the_detail_declares` — both halves, in the shape of `the_pane_gives_up_what_the_window_bar_took` (`:787-812`) | delete the `for cmd in detail.commands` loop from `src/shell/desktop.rs` → red; delete `.chrome-actions` from `assets/desktop.css` → red |
| **NEW** `every_destination_has_a_captured_desktop_state` — reads `docs/gallery-states.json`, asserts every `nav::DESTINATIONS` id has ≥1 key starting `desktop-<id>`, and asserts `seen > 0` | delete the 14 `desktop-*` keys from the store → red. **Today that same deletion leaves `node docs/audit.js both` printing `Clean` and exiting 0**, with the desktop grid silently absent from the summary, because `docs/audit.js:1760` is `[false, ...(count(true) ? [true] : [])]` — built from whether any desktop state happens to exist rather than from anything observed. Verified satisfiable at HEAD: `chats`→`desktop-chats`, `code`→`desktop-code-list`, `recipes`→`desktop-recipes-list`, `skills`→`desktop-skills`, `scheduler`→`desktop-scheduler`, `extensions`→`desktop-extensions`, `settings`→`desktop-settings`. |
| **NEW** the `.shell` guard in `docs/audit.js` | rename `.shell` to `.frame` consistently in the desktop states. Today the run reports `Clean` while quietly losing two of its three shell cells — `data-nav` and `data-fullscreen` are set on `.shell` at `:1696-1699`, and the summary at `:1755-1758` goes on claiming three cells because it is built from `DESKTOP_SHELL.length`. After, it throws. |
| `node docs/audit.js both` → Clean, on the re-captured store | **`DRAG-GONE`**: give `.chrome-actions` `flex: 1 1 auto` so it eats the drag strip → `docs/audit.js:1159` fires below 44px. **`TITLE-COLLIDE`**: `margin-left: -40px` on `.chrome-actions` → `:1051` fires. Both already run against the band's stress variants (`LONGEST['.chrome-heading']` and `['.chrome-sub']` at `:673-674`, doubled into the corpus at `:1540`), so the new buttons are measured against the longest title in the corpus at 480×560 with no new stress entry. |
| **the phone**: `git diff docs/gallery-states.json` names only `desktop-*` keys | that diff *is* the byte-comparison, in the form a reviewer can read |

### The check that proves it did something

`the_window_bar_paints_the_commands_the_detail_declares`, plus the audit's TITLE-COLLIDE on `.chrome-actions` at 480×560 against the stressed title. The first proves the wire is connected in Rust *and* in CSS; the second proves the resulting box is somewhere a person can use, at the window floor, with the worst title in the corpus. Neither can pass with the feature absent.

### Capture

Desktop half only: `cargo run -p mock-goose-server`, `cargo run > /tmp/desktop.log`, drive the states, `scripts/capture-gallery.py --merge /tmp/desktop.log`. ~15 states now, not 14 — **`desktop-code-chat` is captured in this commit**, because the store has no Code detail state at all today (`desktop-code-list` is the only `code` key), so the second command would otherwise be declared and never rendered by anything the grid walks. `--merge` prints every carried-over phone key on stderr, which is exactly the warning a reviewer should see and not act on.

## 4. THE SEQUENCE

| # | stage | compresses? | notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| A | **the command primitive + the band paints it** (§3) | no | one new file, one shell hunk, one sheet block |
| B | **the checks that watch the desktop** | to one agent | see below |
| C | **`.layer` — the anchored popover** | **no** | the vocabulary stage; two agents inventing two positioned layers is the worst outcome available |
| D | **depth inside destinations** | half | Code's stack; Settings' section index |
| E | **the menu bar** | no | one `src/main.rs` hunk + one `src/platform/menu.rs` |
| F | **the composer's satellites** | code yes, capture no | the phone-capture boundary |
| G | **the nav's live chats feed, and per-destination column count** | yes, one agent | **first irreversible decision** |
| H | **the deck — N live sessions** | **no** | `src/state.rs`, last |

**Stage B — the checks that watch the desktop.** Two of its three items landed in commit A (the `.shell` guard, the destination-coverage test); B finishes the job and captures what the grid is missing. It adds the desktop-half store reader in P3's shape — walk every `desktop-`-keyed state, assert what the desktop's markup must and must not contain, assert `seen > 0`. Today **no test in this repo reads a desktop state**: `the_phone_drawer_gains_no_attribute` (`src/shell/mod.rs:305-334`) and `shipped_markup` (`src/views/chrome.rs:521-543`) both filter the desktop half *out*. B also captures the four Code detail screens the store has never held. One agent, because it is two files.

**Stage C — `.layer`.** Ordered by one measurement taken *before* any of it is written: `CSS.supports('anchor-name: --x')` in the shipped WKWebView, via one `document::eval` on a `cargo run` session. Measured here, in the browser that gates this — `chromium.launch()` at `docs/audit.js:57`, HeadlessChrome/151.0.7922.34 — `anchor-name`, `position-anchor`, `position-area`, `container-type` and `popover` are all `true`. Playwright's webkit is not installed on this machine, so the shipped engine is genuinely unverified. This matters more than it looks: `docs/audit.js:1603` navigates to a file holding captured markup plus `<link>` stylesheets and **runs no app JS**, so a CSS-anchored popover is inside the grid and a JS-positioned one is measured at its CSS default forever. That is the same argument the tree already uses to disqualify drag-to-resize. The named fallback if the measurement says false: `.layer` renders at a CSS default and one single-shot `document::eval` at open time writes `--anchor-x/--anchor-y` — legal under constraint 3 (one DOM event), and the cost is stated rather than hidden, because the audit then checks "does it fit where it defaults" and not "does it land on its trigger". `.layer` is a child of `.shell` and therefore inside `.app`, which is what `src/domdump.rs:34-36` serialises — a popover outside `.app` is disqualified by constraint 5 by construction. `src/domdump.rs`'s `suffix()` (`:40-60`) gains a `[data-surface]` scan, and `scripts/capture-gallery.py`'s `LABELS` gains the keys; this is the exact hazard `src/domdump.rs:28-33` describes, where a new surface silently replaces the base state under the same key. C is also where the row overflow stops being a 560pt card 1,224pt from its `⋯` (`assets/desktop.css:1145-1159`), where `Command` gains `danger`, and where rename/delete finally reach the band — because the state they need is being moved here anyway.

**Stage D — depth inside destinations.** Two `nav.rs` hunks and one new view. Code's `root` (`nav.rs:268`) becomes stack-aware, which fixes a **live bug**: on `CodeScreen::Diff` and `::Pulls` (`nav.rs:279-286`) the detail column shows the diff while the list column unconditionally shows `CodeSessionsView`, so the chat being reviewed is off screen entirely and the only way back is the chevron at `views/code.rs:1636`. Settings' `root` (`nav.rs:431`) becomes a section index, which is more Mac-shaped than the reference's own answer (a horizontal `TabsList` at `SettingsView.tsx:158-215`). **Both are phone-invisible and the reason is exact:** `Destination::screen` (`nav.rs:204-209`) is `detail.map(…).or_else(|| root.map(…))`, `or_else` is lazy, and both destinations return `Some` detail in exactly the states that change. Zero phone nodes differ. **Two traps, both already armed:** Settings gaining a root trips `every_destination_with_a_list_can_be_refreshed_by_name` (`src/shell/desktop.rs:899-912`), because `refresh_named` (`src/viewport.rs:423-463`) has arms for `chats`, `code`, `diff`, `pulls`, `extensions`, `skills`, `recipes` and `scheduler` and **none for `settings`**; and `every_destination_but_settings_lists_something` (`nav.rs:537-547`) becomes `every_destination_lists_something`, a strictly stronger assertion. Half-compresses: the Code fix is one hunk, Settings is a new view file, and both land in the same `nav.rs` region.

**Stage E — the menu bar.** `src/main.rs:84-86` is `Config::new().with_window(window)` and never calls `with_menu`, so the app ships tao's default Window+Edit bar. The Go section is generated from `nav::DESTINATIONS`; `Command` gains `accel: Option<&'static str>` as a declaration the menu renders, with a `no_two_commands_share_a_chord` test. The three `document::eval` strings stay as they are — this app builds with `build(&window)` rather than `build_as_child`, so web content still sees the chord first and the JS listeners survive beside the menu items.

**Stage F — the composer's satellites.** `ui/desktop/src/components/bottom_menu/` is six files — `BottomMenuAlertPopover.tsx`, `BottomMenuExtensionSelection.tsx`, `ContextWindowIndicator.tsx`, `CostTracker.tsx`, `DirSwitcher.tsx`, `ExtensionMenu.tsx` — plus `@`/`/` autocomplete and diagnostics. Each is one `&[Command]`, one popover and (mostly) one protocol wrapper. **The code compresses six ways; the capture does not.** `scripts/capture-gallery.py:16-24` replaces the store wholesale, so six agents cannot each re-capture: this is a *batch* with one capture at the end. It is also the first stage that edits `views/chat.rs`'s markup, so it owes the physical-device run of all 49 phone states — planned as one batch so one device run pays for six surfaces.

**Stage G — the nav's live chats feed, and per-destination column count. This is the first irreversible decision.** Everything before it is additive; this one changes what the window looks like at every width. The feed is `NavigationPanel.tsx:317-408` — a collapsible CHATS section filling the nav's remaining height — and adopting it naively puts **two session lists on screen at once** in a three-column window, one of them the thing the other column exists to be. The reference does not have that problem because it collapsed its content area to make room. So the feed lands together with `beside_detail: bool` on `nav::Destination`: Chats runs one content column with its sessions in the nav, and Code, Recipes, Skills, Scheduler and Extensions keep the two they have. That is reference-first's §7(e) recovery promoted to the design, which is where it belonged. Three documented traps: the feed must **not** write `ctx.drawer_open` (`src/shell/desktop.rs:362-371` — `render_group` closes it on every navigation, and `src/views/scheduler.rs:110` reads it as "an overlay covers this list" and idles the poll for the life of the window); it needs its own fetch of `ctx.sessions`, because the existing one is `use_arrival_refresh` keyed on the destination (`:315-322`), so the list is only fetched when you *go* to Chats; and `render_group` (`src/shell/mod.rs:231-264`) stays byte-frozen — the feed is a **sibling** inside `.navcard`, not a change to the loop.

**Stage H — the deck.** N live sessions. `src/state.rs:687` is already one pump over one WebSocket and background sessions already reach us; `:691-694`'s `if !is_current { continue; }` and the `is_current` guards in `apply_update` are what drop them. So this is a `Signal<HashMap<String, ChatState>>` beside `ctx.chat`, not the reference's ten mounted-and-hidden `BaseChat`s (`ChatSessionsContainer.tsx:57-80`), whose whole purpose is keeping per-component SSE alive over a transport we do not have. Last, deliberately: `use_app_ctx_provider` is the one function every live worktree merges into. Three known collisions to solve there: `ctx.chat_draft` and `ctx.attachments` are one-per-app rather than one-per-conversation, and `SCROLL_ID` is the fixed `"chat-scroll"` (`views/chat.rs:24`) that two mounted transcripts would collide on.

**What does not compress, at any stage: the capture.** ~15 desktop states, 1500ms settle each (`src/domdump.rs:63-64`), one operator, no automation — wry exposes no CDP port and `scripts/verify/` holds nothing that drives the app. `--merge` is the desktop's normal mode and that is a written policy, not a habit.

---

## 5. WHAT THE PHONE GETS, AND WHAT IT COSTS

**Stages A through E and G cost the phone nothing, and it is checkable rather than promised.** Every file they touch is either compiled out of a phone binary — `src/shell/desktop*` by `src/shell/mod.rs:36-39`, and `assets/desktop.css` by `src/css.rs:97-98`, whose emptiness on a phone is asserted **at compile time on the target it is about** by `const _: () = assert!(SHELL.is_empty());` at `src/css.rs:105-106` — or is read by the phone through a path that never reaches the new code:

- `nav::Detail::commands` — `Destination::screen` (`nav.rs:204-209`) reads `.view` and nothing else. `commands` carries the same `#[cfg_attr(phone, expect(dead_code))]` as `crumb` (`:80-87`), and `expect` rather than `allow` is the gate: the day a phone view reads it, the exception is unfulfilled and `cargo check --target aarch64-apple-ios` under CI's `-D warnings` reddens.
- `nav.rs:268` and `nav.rs:431` (Stage D) — `root` changes on destinations whose `detail` is `Some` in the states that matter, and `or_else` is lazy. Zero phone nodes differ.
- `src/domdump.rs` (Stage C) — the `[data-surface]` scan affects **keys**, not markup, and finds nothing on a phone.

The three tests that hold the phone stay armed and unmodified: `the_phone_drawer_gains_no_attribute` (`src/shell/mod.rs:305-334`, which walks every `<button class="drawer-item` in the phone half and forbids a `title=`), `the_phone_row_action_still_matches_the_markup_that_shipped` (`src/views/chrome.rs:481`), and the `session-item on` prohibition (`:554`). `src/views/` keeps its zero-`target_os` invariant: `grep -rn target_os src/views/` returns nothing across 8,158 lines, and it stays that way.

**Stage F costs one device run and there is no way around it**, because it edits `views/chat.rs`'s composer markup. 49 states, ten of them `-swiped` variants needing real drag gestures on a scroll-snap scroller, 1500ms settle each. That is the honest price of the six most valuable features on the list, paid once — which is why F is planned as a batch.

**Stage H is the one that can hurt the phone at runtime rather than in markup.** Fanning background session updates costs battery on a device in a pocket, and `state.rs:691-694` is currently what stops it. So the fan-out is shell-conditional in the house pattern — a `const fn fans_background_updates(shell: Shell) -> bool` beside `nav_tooltip`, `nav_is_active`, `row_action_words` and `row_is_marked` — so both arms run in one host `cargo test`.

**The standing weakening, named rather than discovered.** With `--merge` as the desktop's normal mode, the phone half of the store is compared to itself, so `shipped_markup` (`src/views/chrome.rs:521-543`) — one-directional `contains`, as its own comment says — catches the *loss* of a pinned string only when a phone capture actually happens. The mitigation is policy plus one test: the phone half is re-captured on its own schedule, every stage that touches a phone-rendered node blocks on it (F is the only one that does), and commit A's `every_destination_has_a_captured_desktop_state` is what stops the *other* half of that failure — a merge run that captured nothing and still exited 0.

### Three findings for the phone, produced by reading the reference for the desktop

1. **`prefers-reduced-motion` is emulated by nothing, and it moves geometry.** `emulateMedia` is called with `{ colorScheme }` alone at `docs/audit.js:1595`, `docs/measure-ptr.js:50` and `docs/measure-scroll-bottom.js:276`. `assets/main.css` has three reduced-motion blocks (`:542`, `:2263`, `:4373`) and one changes a **transform**: `.scroll-bottom`'s resting position is `translate(-50%, 8px)` at `:2247` and `translate(-50%, 0)` at `:2263-2267`. That is an 8px vertical difference in a 44px tap target that no run has ever measured, on either shell. Playwright supports `reducedMotion`; adding it is a second theme-shaped axis, not free — and it is a phone gap before it is a desktop one.
2. **The composer's shedding rule is a container-width problem, and the reference already solved it.** `ChatInput.tsx:320-333` runs a `ResizeObserver` on the bottom bar **itself** and drops everything between `DirSwitcher` and `Microphone` below 480px, so the model selector and Send always survive. That is exactly the failure `docs/measure-composer.js` hunts at 360, and our composer already has six chips. `container-type: inline-size` is supported in the browser that gates this (measured above), expresses it with no JS and no resize listener, and is therefore *legal* where the reference's `ResizeObserver` would not be under constraint 2. It is the phone's composer that needs it first.
3. **`.session-ask` has never been captured on either shell.** `src/domdump.rs:53-56` has had a detector since it was written and `docs/audit.js:656`'s unbreakable-URL stress case was authored for it; zero of the 63 states contain one, so that stress case has never fired. The permission-ask card is unaudited on the phone. Stage C's `data-surface` makes that a visible gap rather than a silent one.

---

## 6. THE OPEN QUESTIONS

1. **Chats: one content column or two?** Stage G's `beside_detail` makes this a per-destination choice rather than a global one, and Chats is the row it is genuinely arguable for — the reference has no list column at all, and a live feed in the nav plus a list column at Chats is the same information twice. Say which and G is one flag; leave it and G ships two columns everywhere and the feed is scoped to running sessions only.
2. **What Settings is.** The reference has 16 sections across 15 subdirectories. Stage D builds the index; which sections we actually want behind it is a product decision, and it is where "support basically all of the functionality" turns out to be either five screens or fifty.
3. **When we book the device run.** Stage F is the only stage that owes one, and everything in it is blocked on it. Naming a date makes F a batch with a deadline; not naming one makes F the stage that never lands.
4. **Whether the desktop gets a refresh control.** `src/shell/desktop.rs:292-300` argues deliberately against one and generalises from `SessionListView.tsx`, but `SchedulesView.tsx:483-495` renders a spinning `RefreshCw` with "Refresh"/"Refreshing" labels — in the header of the destination our Scheduler mirrors. Worth settling before Stage E turns ⌘R into a menu item and someone asks why there is no button.

---

## 7. WHAT WE ARE NOT DOING

1. **No second window** — no quick launcher, no session-in-a-new-window, no MCP-app window. Disqualified by constraint 5 *by construction*: `src/domdump.rs:34-36` serialises `document.querySelector('.app').outerHTML` of one window, so a 600×80 frameless always-on-top launcher is not a screen the grid is missing, it is a screen the grid cannot express. It would also cost `AppShell`'s mount-once guarantee (`src/app.rs:78`), which `nav_open` (`src/shell/desktop.rs:377`) and `use_arrival` (`:347-353`) both depend on.
2. **No drag-to-resize on the nav.** Legal under constraint 3 — a `mousemove` is precisely the JS-owned-stream case — and useless under constraint 5, because `docs/audit.js:1603` runs no app JS and a JS-written `--nav-w` would be measured at its CSS default forever. Two enumerated widths (`212` / `72`) that the grid walks beat a continuum nothing checks.
3. **No auto-collapse at a width threshold.** The reference's is hysteresis on a resize stream (`NavigationContext.tsx:93-111`) and no `@media` rule expresses "only on the downward crossing" — constraint 2 disqualifies it outright. Done in JS it would fight the render: `data-nav` is emitted from `nav_open()` on every render of `AppShell` (`src/shell/desktop.rs:420`), so a JS write sticks until the next render and then flips back. An intermittent bug, not a consistent one.
4. **No tab strip in the content area.** It needs `Tab` (`src/state.rs:36-47`) to hold more than one value, which changes `(dest.key)(&ctx)`, which changes every dump key — forcing a full re-capture including the expensive 49.
5. **No MCP-UI apps and no picture-in-picture.** A user-draggable 400×300 floating panel is a `pointermove` stream *and* a positioned layer with no resting geometry to capture, hanging off an `apps` capability we do not have at all.
6. **No persisted desktop preferences.** `src/shell/desktop.rs:17-19` argues for a nav that opens every launch and that argument stands. Separately, and more sharply: `src/state.rs:508-521` records with corroboration that **`use_persistent` does not persist on this app's targets** — it builds over `SessionStorage`, an in-memory `HashMap` off-target — so a preference written in the obvious house style would silently not persist while looking exactly like the code above it. `use_synced_storage::<LocalStorage, _>` is the one that works.
7. **No `crates/goose-native/`.** Nothing in this plan writes `unsafe`, and `unsafe_code = "forbid"` cannot be locally excepted. Create the carve-out crate when context menus or a dock menu arrive, not before.
8. **No `target_os` inside `src/views/`.** Zero occurrences today across 8,158 lines. Every one costs a phone capture, and `src/views/chrome.rs:160-168` spells out the mechanism: Dioxus writes an HTML comment where a false branch would have been, so a runtime branch in shared `rsx!` changes the phone's DOM. There are 474 such placeholders across the 49 captured phone states already. CSS is the cheap divergence and this plan keeps paying in CSS.
9. **No rewrite of the three keyboard listeners.** `REFRESH_KEY`, `DISMISS_KEY` and `NAV_KEY` (`src/shell/desktop.rs:85`, `:132`, `:173`) are three different programs with three separately-argued bodies, they are the app's only Escape route out of a modal, and keyboard behaviour is invisible to the audit grid. Accelerators become declarations the menu bar renders; they never become a generator of these strings.
